sourceStatement:
I completed the prepared Phase 3 target observation protocol on the current bound production surface.

Observed results:

- Chrome native 200% zoom: PASS.
  The child experience remained readable and operable across the activity families and help flow, with no material clipping or unusable layout observed.

- Actual assistive-technology delivery: PASS.
  Windows 11 + Google Chrome + Windows Narrator.
  Math Adventure controls, navigation, task content, answer controls, help and feedback were delivered intelligibly.
  Focus remained usable.
  No unintended duplicate application announcements were observed.
  Normal Chrome/browser UI announcements were distinguishable from the Math Adventure content.

- Actual physically disconnected-device restart: PASS.
  The observation was completed using the prepared exact origin with the local preview stopped and the device externally disconnected.
  The application remained usable after the real device restart and the required synthetic local-state persistence/reopen checks passed.

This is a bounded owner observation only for the actual tested environment.
Do not generalize it into broader device, WCAG, language, educational or real-child certification.
